text_en: In addition to frequently encountered issues—such as unauthorized access to data, excessive or unjustified processing, the use of images through video surveillance systems, unauthorized disclosure of data, or the exercise of data subjects’ rights—the year 2025 brought to the forefront new topics associated with the rapid rhythm of digital transformation.

extraction_note: 157 contraventional acts identified. Also at pages 78 and 90 (144 minutes, 157 contravention facts); extracted once (M3). Romanian version of this passage at about page 11 of the text file (not extracted, M3).

Analysis of the outcomes shows that in 52 cases, the courts upheld the legality of the measures adopted by the NCPDP , thereby validating the Authority’s actions and legal reasoning.

extraction_note: Romanian version of this passage at about page 13 of the text file (not extracted, M3).

text_en: Out of the total minutes on contravention submitted for examination in court during the reference period and previous years, in 130 cases, the courts upheld the validity of the minutes and established contravention liability by applying the corresponding sanctions. At the same time, the courts ordered the termination or annulment of 6 minutes.
summary: Courts upheld 130 NCPDP contravention reports and applied sanctions, and terminated or annulled 6.
extraction_note: The text adds that 137 contravention cases are pending before the courts. Romanian version of this passage at about page 16 of the text file (not extracted, M3).

text_en: The parallel examination, in different procedures – administrative litigation and contravention – of the same findings by the NCPDP continues to represent a structural issue affecting legal predictability and the operational efficiency of the authority. This overlap of procedures generates a high volume of activities requiring human and institutional resources, reducing the authority’s capacity to focus on preventive, educational and systemic supervision activities.
summary: Parallel administrative and contravention proceedings on the same NCPDP findings reduce legal predictability and divert resources from supervision.
extraction_note: Restated with different wording at page 147 (problems section), extracted there. Romanian version of this passage at about page 16 of the text file (not extracted, M3).

text_en: Furthermore, the analysis of case law highlights the persistence of divergent solutions by the courts: in some cases, the findings of the NCPDP are upheld in administrative litigation but overturned in contravention proceedings, or vice versa. This lack of coherence directly affects the efficiency of sanctioning breaches and may lead to a lower level of voluntary compliance by data controllers, contrary to the objective of effective protection of fundamental rights.
summary: Divergent court rulings across the two procedures weaken sanctioning and may lower voluntary compliance by data controllers.
extraction_note: Romanian version of this passage at about page 16 of the text file (not extracted, M3).

text_en: This situation is expected to change with the entry into force of Law No. 195/2024 on personal data protection, which introduces a new mechanism for applying sanctions, namely, the administrative sanction. This legislative framework will allow the authority to apply sanctions directly, in a unified and predictable manner, thereby strengthening the overall effectiveness of the personal data protection mechanism.
summary: Law No. 195/2024 introduces administrative sanctions the NCPDP will apply directly, expected to make sanctioning unified and predictable.
extraction_note: Status adopted: the law is adopted and not yet in force at the time of writing. Hedged: 'is expected to change'. Similar expectation at page 147. Romanian version of this passage at about page 16 of the text file (not extracted, M3).
intervention_as_stated: Law No. 195/2024 on personal data protection (administrative sanction mechanism)

text_en: In the mentioned context, we note that over the course of several years, the NCPDP has addressed the Public Services Agency, the e-Governance Agency and has also informed the Government and the Parliament of the Republic of Moldova, regarding the fact that enabling the connection of the targeted entities contravenes the provisions of Law no. 142/2018 on data exchange and interoperability.

text_en: Regrettably, it is observed that over the last 2 years, according to information presented by the Public Services Agency, only 5 entities have aligned their personal data access operations with the current requirements, while 13 still have access to the main state registries managed by the Public Services Agency via COI technology.

extraction_note: Also 5 entities aligned over the last two years. The count of 13 beneficiaries is also stated earlier on page 111. Romanian version of this passage at about page 37 of the text file (not extracted, M3).

text_en: In this regard, it is relevant to mention the initiative of the e-Governance Agency (ref. no. 300-226 from 12.03.2025), through which it informed the NCPDP that, in accordance with the provisions of Article 8 of Law no. 142/2018, the Interoperability Platform is intended to ensure compliance with data exchange security and confidentiality requirements—a fact which cannot be fully ensured through COI technology in the process of personal data processing.
summary: The e-Governance Agency told the NCPDP that COI technology cannot fully ensure the data security the Interoperability Platform is meant to provide.
extraction_note: The e-Governance Agency's view as reported by the NCPDP. Romanian version of this passage at about page 37 of the text file (not extracted, M3).

text_en: Furthermore, the e-Governance Agency has urgently requested the concerned public authorities to terminate data exchange contracts using COI technology and to undertake measures for the exclusive execution of data exchange through the Interoperability Platform, in order to perform data processing/access operations via methods compatible with security and confidentiality requirements. summary: The e-Governance Agency asked authorities to end COI contracts, exchange data only via MConnect and submit action plans for connection.
extraction_note: Recorded as a recommendation: the Agency asks other authorities to act; the text does not describe a measure adopted. Romanian version of this passage at about page 37 of the text file (not extracted, M3).

text_en: Thus, despite the fact that the involved public entities have been repeatedly notified through multiple requests regarding the urgency of integrating their information systems with the interoperability platform (MConnect), the problem has not been resolved to date, there is no progress, nor have any further actions been taken beyond those previously presented.
summary: Despite repeated requests to integrate with MConnect, the problem of COI access is unresolved and there is no progress.
extraction_note: The sentence follows the Public Services Agency letter of 19.03.2025 and appears to continue its account; attributed to the Agency as reported by the NCPDP. The attribution is not explicit. Romanian version of this passage at about page 37 of the text file (not extracted, M3).

text_en: Therefore, the issue of COI usage remains fully current, under conditions where state authorities/ control bodies continue to access personal data through this technology, which, in fact, does not comply with the requirements for ensuring personal data security during its processing within automated information systems and does not ensure the nominal identification of users who have performed data access operations, despite their obligation to justify the purpose and legal basis of these operations.
summary: State authorities still access personal data via COI, which does not meet security requirements or identify individual users.
extraction_note: Restated with different wording at page 147, extracted there. Romanian version of this passage at about page 38 of the text file (not extracted, M3).
